name_en: Ding Xin Hao "Red Moon" Shu Pu-erh
aliases: Шу пуер Дін Сін Хао Червоний Місяць 2002
processing: Ripe pu-erh: large-leaf maocha fermented in a controlled wet pile, then dried and usually pressed. Retail lots are often sold broken up into small sealed pieces.
harvest_season: Not tied to one picking: ripe pu-erh is a blend of stored maocha. The label gives 2002 as the production year.
appearance_dry: Dark brown compressed ripe leaf, typical of aged factory-style shu.
appearance_liquor: Deep red-brown, as usual for ripe pu-erh with some age.
appearance_wet: Soft dark brown leaf, as usual for ripe pu-erh.
taste_profile: Little independent tasting is on record. The seller's label calls it an 'old Menghai taste', which usually means a smooth, earthy, woody ripe tea with a dark sweetness and any piling aroma long gone.

brewing.notes: Standard ripe handling: one quick rinse to wake up the compressed leaf, then near-boiling water and gradually longer steeps.

vintage_note: Sold in Ukraine as a 2002 ripe pu-erh, including as a piece in shop sampler sets of 'elite' shu. A label vintage this old is the seller's claim and is hard to verify for a lesser-known brand, so treat the year as a guide and judge the tea by the cup: well-aged shu tastes smooth and clean, with no fishy pile smell.
description:
This is a ripe pu-erh sold by Ukrainian tea shops under the name Ding Xin Hao "Red Moon", with 2002 given as its year. Very little about the maker is published, so most of what this card can say comes from the shop label and from how ripe pu-erh in general behaves.

Like all shu, it starts as Yunnan large-leaf tea that is fermented in a warm, damp pile for weeks before pressing. That step turns the leaf dark and the cup smooth and earthy. Twenty-odd years of storage on top of that should take away any rough pile aroma.

The label promises an 'old Menghai taste', meaning the classic factory ripe style: earth, wood, dark sweetness and a thick, soft body. Brew it with very hot water after a quick rinse, and keep the first steeps short because aged compressed leaf gives a lot of colour fast.

When buying, keep in mind that old vintages on little-known labels are hard to confirm. Pay for how the tea tastes rather than for the year on the sticker, and log your sessions here so others can compare.
history: Almost nothing about this tea is documented outside shop listings. The seller's label names it Ding Xin Hao "Red Moon", a Yunnan ripe pu-erh from 2002; the maker, the original pressing and the recipe behind it are not on record.
sources_note: Card written from a photo of the retail label (Ukrainian shop sticker, item code RS-0091-8): 'Шу пуер Дін Сін Хао "Червоний Місяць", Старий менхайський смак, Юньнань, Шу пуер (чорний), 2002 рік'. The sticker also carries 云南易武 (Yunnan Yiwu), which conflicts with 'Menghai taste', so the region is kept at Yunnan. Web search found the same name and year in thetea.ua's 'Еліт' shu sampler set, but the page could not be opened from the writing environment, so it is not listed in sources. Chinese characters and the pinyin of the brand are unconfirmed (searches for 鼎兴号 returned nothing), hence name_native null and a descriptive name_zh. Photo: the team's own shot of the retail package, stored in the repo. Form unknown (bought as a foil-packed piece), so 'other'.
